_what: R10 AS ROWS. One row per OBJECT IN THE FRAME: what it is, whether anything outside this lane says it should be there, whether it could be built and used, and the verdict. Consumed by pipeline/scripts/existence_check.py, which is spawned by build_room after every render and BLOCKS the build.
_law: The object list is DERIVED FROM THE BUILT SCENE (sheet_recon.assemblies_from_dump), never kept here — R9b: a rule that names the objects it applies to will always exempt the next one.

IDENTITY IS SIGNED, CONSEQUENCES ARE MEASURED. No program can look at a box and know it is a drawer, so the row declares; the checker then holds the declaration to the scene — a named support must exist and touch, a claimed reveal must measure, a 'remove' must actually be gone.
`pending` is refused BY NAME. So are `tbd`, `todo` and `later`.
The unrowed backlog RATCHETS and may only fall. A machine that hard-fails every historical instance on day one gets switched off and joins them (R13).
_why_it_exists: R8 governs HOW an object is made and R9 governs WHERE it goes. R10 was written 2026-08-05 because nothing governed WHETHER IT SHOULD EXIST, and on 2026-08-17 two independent critics filed three defects of exactly that class against p2r47 — a foot bench with no load path, drawer fronts with no way to open them, and a room with no skirting, sockets or switches. The round's own triage accepted all three with the same sentence: no instrument in this repo can see it.

required_elements.why_required: A plastered wall meeting a wood floor is not finished without a skirting or a recessed shadow gap; the junction is drawn on every interior elevation. C2 p2r47 item 10: 'no skirting or shadow-gap where wall meets floor on ANY wall'. Height and projection are DR-sourced for the 2700-3200 mm ceiling band (knowledge/_inbox/nlm-th-bedroom-services).

The sconces over the bed are LIT, so something must switch them from somewhere reachable, and a bedroom has sockets. C2 p2r47 item 10: 'no switch plate anywhere, including beside the bed for the sconces; no sockets'. Heights are DR-sourced (door switch 1200-1250 AFFL, bedside switch 600-700, concealed bedside socket 300-350).

objects.identity: The bed: the ACQUIRED whole bed f52472c1 (P2r-52, D-106/D-107 — platform frame with integral side ledges, fitted mattress, one duvet field, 2 pillows + 3 shams, all re-dressed in the six studio bed materials), the sheet-drawn headboard band with welts (R12, stays built), and a measured pillowstop closing the head-end strip. 2000 x 2149 footprint, ink-true.
objects.why: Ink-trued and owner-confirmed; footprint is the client's own drawing (R12). The assembly's construction is acquired per his class order (D-104); the acquired parts group under this row by the bed__ prefix.

objects.identity: Foot-of-bed bench — ONE acquired mesh (Ottoman_01), 498 x 710 in plan, top measured at 501 mm.
objects.fix_by: Give it a visible load path or replace the mesh. Both critics read it as two stacked cushions with nothing to carry the load to the legs, and that is TRUE of this mesh — an upholstered block on an upholstered block. R8 sends the FRAME to the builder (rail + apron + leg = boxes with radii) while the cushion stays acquired; ASK-024 carries the other route, which is a bench of the drawn 498 x 1000 (1:2.0) proportion that the free shelf does not hold.
objects.why: PARTLY REFUTED WITH A MEASUREMENT, and the surviving half is real. C2's 'a seat at mattress height is not a seat' does not hold: the bench top measures 501 mm and the mattress top 600 mm, so it sits 99 mm BELOW the sleeping plane and inside the 400-500 mm seat band it cites. The load-path half stands and no number refutes it.

objects.identity: Bedside table, one acquired mesh (Blendkit 341b04e0 Modern Nightstand 02, greige waterfall), 400 x 400 in plan, top at ~400 mm = sleeping plane - 25 (D-115 re-derivation of D-045's datum relation).
objects.why: Drawn. Its height was raised to the mattress datum at p2r27 on the owner's own order (D-045). MOVED p2r56 from the drawn seat (y 2200) to hug the standard-size bed at a 10 mm slot gap — his order 2026-08-22 verbatim in ORD-2026-08-22-bed-standard-size-hug / D-114; the drawn position served the drawn 7-ft bed that D-114 retired. | RE-KEYED 2026-08-24: the assembly name embeds the piece's PLAN COORDINATE, so carrying out D-115's owner-locked hug numbers (y 2005->2036 / -210->-184, which make the twins symmetric to 0.0 mm against the 57 mm they were) renamed it and orphaned this row. Paid once because the position stays typed; a DERIVED position would re-key it every round, which is why that plan was refused.

objects.identity: Bedside table, one acquired mesh (Blendkit 341b04e0 Modern Nightstand 02, greige waterfall), 400 x 400 in plan, top at ~400 mm = sleeping plane - 25 (D-115 re-derivation of D-045's datum relation).
objects.why: Drawn. Its height was raised to the mattress datum at p2r27 on the owner's own order (D-045). MOVED p2r56 from the drawn seat (y -450) to hug the standard-size bed at a 10 mm slot gap — ORD-2026-08-22-bed-standard-size-hug / D-114. | RE-KEYED 2026-08-24: the assembly name embeds the piece's PLAN COORDINATE, so carrying out D-115's owner-locked hug numbers (y 2005->2036 / -210->-184, which make the twins symmetric to 0.0 mm against the 57 mm they were) renamed it and orphaned this row. Paid once because the position stays typed; a DERIVED position would re-key it every round, which is why that plan was refused. | BROKEN AT p2r60 BY A RESIZE, NOT A MOVE (measured p2r62, 2026-08-24). The r60 model swap changed this item's w/d from 400 to 449 and left x/y untouched — and `y` is the bbox MIN CORNER, so the piece grew NORTHWARD, which is away from the bed for its twin and INTO the bed for this one. BEFORE (400): north 2036..2436, south -184..216, inner faces 910 mm from the bed centre on both sides — symmetric to 0.0 mm, exactly as D-115 claimed. AFTER (449): north 2036..2485 (inner still 910 from centre), south -184..265 (inner 861) — 49 mm asymmetric, and this top now takes 39 mm out of `bed__headboard` (y226..2026, z0..1100, x5144..5204) in all three axes. Nothing failed, because a coordinate is always a legal coordinate: R9's own sentence, reproduced by the round that swapped the model.
objects.fix_by: CONVERT THE PAIR TO A DERIVED MIRROR, DO NOT TYPE A THIRD NUMBER. gate-DELIV001-P2r57 wrote the rule for exactly this moment: 'iterate 2 ครั้ง = ขีดสุด stop-loss R9 — ครั้งหน้าที่ของพวกนี้ขยับ ต้อง convert เป็น contact-derived ก่อน ห้าม nudge ครั้งที่สาม'. The relation is: each bedside piece's INNER face sits one gap from the bed's headboard face, mirrored about the bed centre-line — a y-axis `mirror_about`, which placement.py already models on x and would need the axis generalised. The rung that would have caught this is placement_check (R9b), declared blocking in qa/coverage-map.json and never spawned by build_room; it is already filed as room_lane_debt (2026-08-24).

objects.identity: The two bedside table lamps, mirror twins: base, stem, spun brass dome shade, and the bulb the dome encloses (millwork.nightstand_lamp_parts + nightstand_lamp_emitter_z, one definition for the mesh and the light, D-125).
objects.exists: not-in-drawing: element 8 / D3 styling — the furniture plan draws a 300 mm lamp circle on each bedside carcass (pen 0.12, measured from the strokes 2026-08-24) but carries no elevation, so the lamp is IN the drawing in plan and its form is ours
objects.why: A bedside table with a lamp is what the spec's own item name says it is ('โต๊ะข้างเตียง (มีโคมไฟ)'), and each lamp rests on the measured top of its own table. ONE ROW COVERS BOTH TWINS because their justification is one sentence twice — they are mirror instances of a single decision, not two objects with two reasons. | RE-KEYED TWICE IN ONE DAY, AND THAT IS WHY THE KEY IS NOW A PREFIX (p2r62, 2026-08-24). The first re-key (04:00, from D-115's owner-locked hug) was TYPED: the lamp's new coordinate was obtained by adding the TABLE's move to the lamp's old number instead of reading the built scene, and it landed on @4869,2102 while the dump said @4869,2102 — correct that morning by luck of the arithmetic. The second break needed no move at all: D-125 gave millwork the one definition of the dome and its bulb, and the rebuilt shade is 80.2 mm taller with its plan min 8.2 mm in on both axes, so the assembly renamed itself to @4877,2110 / @4877,-109 and BOTH rows orphaned. MEASURED across the round series (existence_check re-run standalone on each scene dump): r59 clean, r60 clean, r61 2 unrowed, r62 2 unrowed — so p2r61 shipped a BUILD FAILED frame and the round was reported closed, because the orchestrator prints the failure and exits 0 (the same confession the p2r57 gate artifact already wrote down). | THE KEY IS THE DEFECT, not the numbers: an existence row answers WHAT IS IT / DOES IT EXIST / DOES IT MAKE SENSE, and none of those three answers change when a shade grows 80 mm. Position is R9's question and placement_check is its rung. existence_check's own comment prescribes exactly this repair — a bare-prefix row covers every component of the prefix — and the prefix form is strictly MORE checked than the coordinate form was: `held_by` is touch-tested only when the row key resolves in `by_name`, which is prefix-keyed, so neither coordinate row had ever had its load path measured.

objects.identity: The pelmet's north return, closing its end against the wall.

objects.identity: Recessed downlight trim ring, 96 mm, sitting in the ceiling plane.
objects.why: RESOLVED p2r49/p2r50, and the R10 rung is what found it. Filed unresolved when this ledger opened: the trim sat at z 2734-2740 under a 2800 soffit, so every recessed can in the room hung 60 mm below the ceiling it is recessed into, on every frame this lane has shipped. THE CAUSE was one parameter carrying two things — `_recessed_trim` was handed the FIXTURE's z, and the fixture sits at `ceiling - 60` because an emitter coplanar with the geometry it lights self-shadows. That stand-off is right for the light and wrong for the trim. The light keeps it; the geometry now takes the ceiling. Measured after the fix: trim 2794.0-2799.5 under a 2800.0 soffit (a 5.5 mm flange, flush), aperture 2790.0-2793.0 recessed 7-10 mm above it.

objects.identity: Skirting: a 100 x 15 mm painted band where a plastered wall meets the oak floor, run along the room outline and stopped at every doorway and at every floor-standing mass that backs onto that wall.

objects.identity: Wall services: an 86 x 86 mm faceplate beside the bedroom door at 1225 mm AFFL (the room switch), and per bedside a switch at 700 mm and a socket plate at 325 mm on the bed-head wall.
objects.exists: not-in-drawing: a furniture plan carries no electrical; heights are DR-sourced Thai residential practice (D-098's same unit)
objects.why: C2 p2r47 item 10, and its grounding is the sharpest R10 sentence either critic wrote: the sconces over the bed are LIT, so they must be switched from somewhere reachable. Every position is derived from the opening or the nightstand it serves, so moving the door moves the switch. The carrier is named as the CLASS 'wall' and not as one mass because the three plates sit on three DIFFERENT walls — the door switch on the east wall, the two bedside plates on the BF14 slat wall standing in front of it. The checker refused the first draft of this row, which named wall_4: the plate is nowhere near it. NOTE p2r49: filed as FIX on the day it was built — the blind critic caught the mounting detail in the first frame it appeared in, which is the ladder working rather than a defect surviving.
objects.fix_by: Give each faceplate a flat MOUNTING BLOCK behind it. C2 filed it against the very object this round added (p2r49 item 16: "the switch plate floats on the slat wall with no mounting block, recess or shadow") and it is right as construction: the plate spans x5193-5203, i.e. it lands flush with the slat faces and bridges the gaps between them, and you cannot screw a faceplate to a slat. A real installation cuts the slats back to a flat plaster or ply pad. The pad is a box with radii, so R8 sends it to the builder.

objects.identity: RESOLVED 2026-08-24 - not a wire and not a separate object: the vertical SHADOW REVEAL between the millwork tall unit's end panel and the painted wall, at the frame's extreme left. Named from p2r54's OWN MATMASK (the probe that filed this row used the idmask, whose roster was bed-focused and returned id 0): 84 of the line's 106 pixels carry material id 39 = m_millwork_oak_veneer_photo, the remainder antialiasing between palette levels, with ceiling_paint (id 14) in the adjacent column x=21. The small metallic cone just below it at x~17 y~94 is a THIRD material, e5_trim_dark (id 20) - the E5 pelmet trim. Both surfaces belong to assemblies this ledger already carries.
objects.exists: not-in-drawing: a shadow gap is a millwork DETAIL rather than a mass, so no sheet rect can correspond to it; it is there because the tall unit's end panel stops short of the wall, which is the reveal the millwork is built with
objects.why: R10 question 1 is answered and the answer changes the verdict: nothing here is an unexplained mass. C2 (p2r54, blind-local) was RIGHT about the pixels - a thin dark line descending from the top edge - and wrong only about what makes them, which is what a blind critic is for. What failed was the BUILDER's probe. Two errors, both measurable today: (1) its recorded coordinates do not hold the feature. It wrote 'a black angular mass ~40 px at x 30-45, y 150-230 of 2400x1800'; that window in p2r54 measures min luma 0.6549, mean 0.6799, and contains ZERO pixels below 0.10. The real feature is a ONE-PIXEL-WIDE column at x=22 spanning y 0-105 - 100 px below 0.10, all in a single column, which is why an 'angular mass' was the wrong shape to look for. (2) it asked the idmask, got id 0 over the region, and stopped - while the MATMASK for the same frame sat beside it on disk and names the material in one query. The hanger-hook hypothesis it reached instead is refuted: no hanger is within 1500 mm of the frame's left margin, and the pixels are oak veneer. VERDICT keep: a shadow reveal between millwork and wall is a deliberate detail, the millwork run stands on the floor, and there is nothing to remove. NOT A CLAIM THAT WE FIXED IT: the feature is absent from p2r62 and p2r64 only because the eye camera MOVED after p2r55 (floor_poly_mm differs between the p2r54 and p2r58 dumps), so it is out of frame, not corrected. If the camera returns to p2r54's station the reveal returns with it, and it is legitimate when it does. The assembly key keeps its filed name so the history stays greppable (law 4: rows never leave the ledger). Filed p2r54, mis-probed p2r55, resolved from the matmask 2026-08-24.

objects.identity: The flat sheet of the ACQUIRED Metropol bed set (e2418055) — the layer between the mattress and the blanket. 1,354,622 polys, the heaviest single object in the scene (the duvet is 388k), plan x3273..3849 y78..2157 z81..541.
objects.exists: not-in-drawing: element 3 bedding — the furniture plan draws the bed, not the layers of a made bed (same ground as the pillows and duvet)
objects.fix_by: Give it a ROLE in wholebed_rules so it takes a signed bedding material. Today it is the set's one UNCLASSIFIED part and build_room prints that at every build — 'UNCLASSIFIED part Sheet keeps its imported material' — so it renders a stranger's `Brown textured fabric` against D3-1's signed greige linen family, which is exactly the defect the _CASE_GOODS material policy was written for at p2r37 (*มันใส่วัสดุของตัวเองมา*). MEASURED, so the urgency is not overstated: the duvet's AABB encloses it on every axis except ~28 mm at the hem and ~26-41 mm at the sides, and no brown band is separable in the p2r59q frame — the warm-pixel share of the bed-foot band is 0.84%, which is floor edge. So this is a latent material defect on a part that is currently almost entirely hidden, plus a real 1.35M-poly cost for it.
objects.why: ROWED 2026-08-24, and it is a backlog row rather than a new object: existence_check exits 0 on the p2r57 dump and 1 on p2r58, so the Metropol bed brought this part in at p2r58 (d57ea4f) and that round was committed with this blocking gate failing. Rowing it is not approving it — the verdict is `fix` and the action is named.
